=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: .github/workflows/implement.yml
  Location: lines 3669–3670, within the scope-block handler's latch-verification block
  Issue: The pre-initialized `SCOPE_LATCH_STATUS_LINE` and `SCOPE_TG_LATCH_LINE` assignments are dead defaults. Every execution path through the `if/elif/else` ladder overwrites them: the success path (line 3672-3673), the "label not found" path (lines 3685-3686), and the "gh issue view failed" path (already sets its own value on lines 3685-3686). No branch falls through to use lines 3669-3670.
  Why it matters: These dead defaults create operator-facing ambiguity — a future reader might assume the pre-set values define the failure fallback behavior, when in fact the else block at lines 3685-3686 is the real fallback. They are harmless at runtime but are misleading and fragile.
  Suggested minimal fix: Remove lines 3669-3670 (the two `SCOPE_LATCH_STATUS_LINE=` / `SCOPE_TG_LATCH_LINE=` defaults) so initialization only happens where the value is actually used. Estimated lines changed: -2.
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 0
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: .github/workflows/implement.yml
  Line or code reference: 3679-3696 (the `if scope_latched_labels=...` block and variable re-assignments)
  Problem: The three `SCOPE_*_LINE` variables are initialized with the read-failure / "not confirmed blocked" messages before the `gh issue view`. The `else` branch (read failure) and the `if grep` failure branch re-assign them, but the re-assignments in the `else` path duplicate the default, making the explicit "follow-up label read failed" path unreachable in some flows.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operator messaging and Telegram alerts can emit stale or contradictory text when `gh issue view` fails after the best-effort write (network flake, rate-limit, token scope, etc.). The destructive-blocked handler (lines ~3769) does not suffer this exact reassignment pattern.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: .github/workflows/implement.yml
  Line or code reference: 3669 (initialization of `SCOPE_LATCH_STATUS_LINE` / `SCOPE_TG_LATCH_LINE`) and the three `else` / failure branches that re-assign them
  Problem: The read-failure path is initialized but then overwritten in every branch, so the explicit fallback message "The workflow attempted to label this issue `ai:scope-blocked`, but the follow-up label read failed..." is never emitted. The `::warning::` and Telegram lines are also inconsistent with the intent stated in the linked issue.
  Why it fails at runtime: When the post-write verification read fails (realistic under GH API flakiness), operators receive a generic "verification failed" message instead of the precise "not confirmed blocked — re-check manually" that the issue #3599 required. The test `test_scope_alert_step_verifies_latch_after_write` only checks for substring presence and therefore does not catch the unreachable-code smell.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
